title-proc.eng: TR5866 A Single Supplier Framework Agreement Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services pursuant to a framework agreement

description-proc.eng: The Contracting Entity intends to procure a Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services framework for the provision of specialist digital learning services, including instructional design, eLearning development, accessibility reviews, project management and associated support services. The successful tenderer will be required to work collaboratively with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to design, develop, review, test and deliver digital learning content from initial onboarding through to final approval and provision of SCORM-compliant outputs. The supplier will be expected to provide a structured and transparent development methodology, supported by appropriate governance, project management, universal design principles including accessibility, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement processes. It is proposed that the Framework will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): Create engaging, accessible and effective digital learning that keeps learner needs, content and learning objectives central to the design. Examples of digital learning topics and types include: Policy, process or compliance learning Systems, technical or operational training Bite-sized learning, such as microlearning, video or animation Develop digital learning materials using the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation) framework, ensuring learning objectives, activities and assessments align with Bloom’s Taxonomy and the needs of the target audience. Use purposeful interactive approaches to enhance learner engagement. Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and accessibility by design principles throughout, ensuring compliance with WCAG 2.2, EN 301 549 and ESB accessibility requirements, and meeting accessibility best practices. Ensure all interactive elements are accessible, usable and support diverse learner needs, undertaking additional development where required to meet accessibility requirements. Undertake accessibility testing as part of the design, development and quality assurance process, using appropriate testing methods and tools, and remediate identified accessibility issues prior to final delivery and approval. Provide appropriate coaching, guidance and instructional design support to SMEs within the business. Project manage the end-to-end development of digital learning solutions, from the business’s SME onboarding to final delivery, including appropriate project planning, timelines, milestones, review stages, change management and stakeholder approval/sign-off. Provide user friendly collaboration tools that enable SMEs to review content, give feedback, track changes and monitor progress. Apply internal governance and quality assurance controls to ensure all deliverables meet ESB’s scope, requirements, timelines and quality standards. Provide access to a library of pre-existing digital learning modules on standard or commonly required topics (e.g. data protection, cybersecurity, health and safety, compliance or similar). Where appropriate, these modules should be capable of reasonable customisation to incorporate ESB branding, accessibility requirements and organisation-specific information. Digital learning content must be developed using a recognised, globally adopted authoring tool (e.g. Articulate 360 or equivalent). Provide all content in a SCORM-compliant format. Ensure compatibility with ESB’s current Learning Management System (SuccessFactors) on desktop, mobile and tablet devices. Provide access to a dedicated team with the skills and capacity required to deliver services to ESB, including an ESB Account Lead, Instructional Designers, eLearning Developers, QA/Accessibility Specialists, Project Managers and additional creative team e.g. Graphic Designers/ Illustrators and Animators.

title-proc.eng: 10024519-Capacity building and support for National Forest Inventory in Indonesia

description-proc.eng: Indonesia"s tropical forests are critical for global climate stability, yet they face widespread threats from unsustainable land-use practices, illegal logging, and forest fires, which cause significant deforestation and high Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions. While the Government of Indonesia aims for a 29% carbon emission cut by 2030 and has fostered new policies through decentralization, the key challenge remains implementation at the regional and provincial level. Differences in technical capacity, resource allocation, and inter-sectoral coordination may affect the consistency of monitoring, law enforcement, and sustainable forest management (SFM) planning required to support national commitments. The FORCLIME project aims to achieve two objectives (1) Climate Mitigation: To significantly reduce GHG emissions from the forestry sector and (2) Livelihood Strengthening: To strengthen local livelihoods without undermining conservation efforts. The FORCLIME project collaborates with the Indonesian Ministry of Forestry on national forest policy and sector strategies, as well as on the subnational implementation of activities to support local forest management. At subnational level the project operates in eastern Indonesia in the provinces of Central Sulawesi, Papua, and South West Papua and South Papua. The project directly addresses implementation gaps by building technical capacity and improving cross-sectoral coordination within provincial and national authorities, ensuring the effective execution of forest conservation and SFM policy on the ground. Effective local stakeholder participation is a critical success factor in all planning and strategy development processes.

title-proc.nld: Vrijwillige transparantie - Direct onderhandelen - Relinen werkpakket gas
title-proc.eng: Voluntary Ex Ante Transparency Announcement for the relinen gas work package

description-proc.nld: Deze vrijwillige aankondiging overeenkomstig artikel 4.16 Aanbestedingswet 2012 betreft het voornemen van Alliander N.V. om met inzet van de onderhandelingsprocedure zonder aankondiging op grond van artikel 3.36 lid 1 sub c onder 2 Aanbestedingswet 2012 een raamovereenkomst te sluiten met Van Gelder Kabel‑, Leiding‑ en Montagewerken B.V. ten behoeve van het werkpakket relinen gas van Alliander met een totale looptijd van zes jaar. Achtergrond en doelstelling Bij relinen wordt de binnenkant van een grijs gietijzeren gasleiding gerenoveerd met een gelijmde kous. Alliander is voornemens grijs gietijzeren gasleidingen te relinen wanneer traditioneel saneren niet de voorkeur heeft (bijvoorbeeld in dicht stedelijke gebieden). Dit zorgt voor minder omgevingshinder en een hogere productiviteit.   Reden van vrijwillige transparantie vooraf Alliander N.V. is voornemens om middels de onderhandelingsprocedure zonder aankondiging op grond van artikel 3.36 lid 1 sub c onder 2 Aanbestedingswet 2012 een raamovereenkomst te sluiten met Van Gelder Kabel‑, Leiding‑ en Montagewerken B.V. ten behoeve van het werkpakket relinen gas van Alliander met een initiële looptijd van vier jaar en twee keer mogelijkheid tot verlenging van een jaar. De totale looptijd van de beoogde is overeenkomst is daarmee zes jaar. Uit marktonderzoek van Alliander is gebleken dat Van Gelder Kabel‑, Leiding‑ en Montagewerken B.V. de enige partij is die binnen afzienbare tijd invulling kan geven aan dit werkpakket en daarnaast aan de eisen en specificaties van Alliander voldoen en over de juiste kwalificaties beschikt. Deze zijn noodzakelijk om de kwaliteit en veiligheid te waarborgen. Technische en operationele eisen Voor de uitvoering van het werkpakket Relinen Gas stelt Alliander eisen die voortvloeien uit de kritische aard van de gasinfrastructuur, de omvang van het werkpakket en de benodigde continuïteit van de saneringsopgave. De opdrachtnemer dient onder meer: • aantoonbare ervaring te hebben met het relinen van grijs gietijzeren gasleidingen middels de naadloze kousmethode; • te beschikken over bewezen kennis van het Nederlandse gasnet en de bijbehorende veiligheids- en kwaliteitsvereisten; • te beschikken over de voor de werkzaamheden vereiste certificeringen, bevoegdheden en veiligheidskwalificaties (NTA 8032:2016 NL, VIAG-aanwijzing, of vergelijkbare kwalificaties); • de werkzaamheden op korte termijn en op landelijke schaal binnen het verzorgingsgebied van Alliander te kunnen uitvoeren; te beschikken over voldoende direct in te zetten gekwalificeerd personeel, gespecialiseerd materieel en een ingerichte uitvoeringsorganisatie voor reliningwerkzaamheden met een naadloze kous; • aantoonbaar in staat te zijn de vereiste productieaantallen en capaciteitsvraag op korte termijn te realiseren; te voldoen aan de eisen ten aanzien van kwaliteitsborging volgens CKB en ISO 9001:2015 (of gelijkwaardig) en revisiegegevens overeenkomstig de WIBON en de in bijlage G.1.1 opgenomen ‘Aanlevereisen ondergrondse revisie v2.4’ van Liander aan te leveren (deze is te vinden en te downloaden in Mercell); • Diameters van de leidingen die door middel van relinen van een naadloze kous voorzien dienen te worden: DN 150/ DN 200 / DN 250 / DN 300 / DN 400 / DN 600. Geen redelijk alternatief of substituut Uit het door Alliander uitgevoerde marktonderzoek is gebleken dat meerdere marktpartijen interesse hebben in reliningwerkzaamheden. Tegelijkertijd is vastgesteld dat slechts één partij op dit moment aantoonbaar beschikt over de combinatie van benodigde ervaring, beschikbare capaciteit, operationele inrichting en kwalificaties. Deze partij beschikt daarnaast over de directe beschikbaarheid om het volledige werkpakket binnen de gestelde voorwaarden uit te voeren. Op basis hiervan concludeert Alliander dat er momenteel geen redelijk alternatief of substituut beschikbaar is waarmee tijdig aan de technische en operationele eisen van het werkpakket kan worden voldaan. Bezwaar Indien u bezwaar heeft tegen de voorgenomen gunning van de opdracht aan Van Gelder Kabel‑, Leiding‑ en Montagewerken B.V., althans van mening bent dat met voornoemde gunning ten onrechte een beroep gedaan is op een uitzonderingsgrond, kunt u uw bezwaren kenbaar maken door een kort geding aanhangig te maken binnen twintig (20) kalenderdagen na de datum van deze publicatie. Indien dat niet gebeurt, kan de hierboven beschreven overeenkomst tot stand worden gebracht en kunnen dergelijke bezwaren niet meer leiden tot aantasting (vernietiging) van de overeenkomst.
description-proc.eng: This voluntary transparency announcement in accordance with Article 4.16 of the Public Procurement Act 2012 concerns Alliander N.V.'s intention to enter into a framework agreement with Van Gelder Kabel-, Leiding- en Montagewerken B.V. for Alliander's relinen gas work package with a total term of six years, using the negotiated procedure without prior notification pursuant to Article 3.36(1)(c)(2) of the Dutch Public Procurement Act 2012. Background and objective In relining, the inside of a gray cast iron gas pipe is renovated with a glued sleeve. Alliander intends to reline grey cast-iron gas pipes when traditional remediation is not preferred (e.g. in densely urban areas). This ensures less environmental nuisance and higher productivity. Reason for voluntary transparency in advance Alliander N.V. intends to enter into a framework agreement with Van Gelder Kabel-, Leiding- en Montagewerken B.V. for Alliander's relining gas work package with an initial term of four years and two one-year extensions by means of the negotiated procedure without prior publication pursuant to Article 3.36(1)(c)(2) of the Public Procurement Act 2012. The total term of the intended agreement is therefore six years. Market research by Alliander has shown that Van Gelder Kabel-, Leiding- en Montagewerken B.V. is the only party that can implement this work package in the foreseeable future and also meet Alliander's requirements and specifications and has the right qualifications. These are necessary to guarantee quality and safety. Technical and operational requirements For the implementation of the Relinen Gas work package, Alliander sets requirements arising from the critical nature of the gas infrastructure, the scope of the work package and the required continuity of the remediation task. The contractor must, among other things: • have demonstrable experience in relining grey cast iron gas pipes using the seamless sleeving method; • have proven knowledge of the Dutch gas network and the associated safety and quality requirements; • have the certifications, powers and safety qualifications required for the work (NTA 8032:2016 NL, VIAG designation, or comparable qualifications); • to be able to carry out the work in the short term and on a national scale within Alliander's service area; • have a sufficient number of qualified personnel to be deployed immediately, specialised equipment and an established implementation organisation for relining work with a seamless stocking; • be able to demonstrate the ability to achieve the required production numbers and capacity demand in the short term; • to meet the requirements with regard to quality assurance in accordance with CKB and ISO 9001:2015 (or equivalent) and to provide revision data in accordance with the WIBON and Liander's 'Aanlevereisen ondergrondse revisie v2.4' included in Appendix G.1.1. (see Mercell for download); • Diameters of the pipes to be provided with a seamless sleeve by means of relining: DN 150 / DN 200 / DN 250 / DN 300 / DN 400 / DN 600. No reasonable alternative or substitute The market research carried out by Alliander has shown that several market parties are interested in relining work. At the same time, it has been established that only one party currently has the demonstrable combination of required experience, available capacity, operational structure and qualifications. This party also has the immediate availability to carry out the entire work package within the set conditions. On this basis, Alliander concludes that there is currently no reasonable alternative or substitute available that can meet the technical and operational requirements of the work package in a timely manner. Objection If you object to the intended award of the contract to Van Gelder Kabel-, Leiding- en Montagewerken B.V., or if you believe that the aforementioned award wrongly relies on an exception to the procurement rules, you may make your objections known by initiating summary proceedings (kort geding) within twenty (20) calendar days of the date of publication of this notice. If no such proceedings are initiated within this period, the agreement described above may be concluded and such objections can no longer result in the annulment or invalidation of the agreement.

description-proc.fra: Le département « Construction métallique et composite » de l'ETH Zurich prévoit l'acquisition d'une nouvelle machine d'essai universelle pour le hall de construction du site de Hönggerberg. Cette installation est destinée à tester des éléments de construction de grande taille soumis à des charges statiques et dynamiques proches de la réalité, et à soutenir ainsi les futurs travaux de recherche dans les domaines de l’ingénierie de la construction métallique, des structures mixtes et de la résistance aux séismes. Parmi ses principales applications figurent « les essais de compression centrés et excentrés […] avec la possibilité, en option, d’appliquer des forces de traction ». La direction du projet est assurée par Dominik Werne, responsable du hall d’essais. La machine doit offrir un espace d’essai spacieux, capable d’accueillir des éprouvettes mesurant jusqu’à « B : 1 500 mm, H : 1 500 mm, L : 5 000 mm ». Des hauteurs de serrage comprises entre 500 et 5 000 mm permettent de réaliser aussi bien des essais de compression que de traction. L’espace d’essai doit être entièrement visible afin de pouvoir utiliser des systèmes de mesure optique tels que le DIC. L'équipement hydraulique comprend un vérin vertical d'une « charge de compression de 10 MN, d'une charge de traction de 6 MN et d'une course de 400 mm », ainsi que deux vérins horizontaux d'une « charge de compression/traction de 1 MN et d'une course de 500 mm » chacun. L'installation doit permettre de réaliser des essais dynamiques jusqu'à 10 Hz et à des vitesses allant jusqu'à 250 mm/s. Une commande précise avec une fréquence d'échantillonnage d'au moins 5 kHz, une classe de qualité 1/0,5 ainsi que des interfaces numériques modernes (par exemple EtherCAT) est nécessaire pour prendre en charge les essais à force et à déformation contrôlées ainsi que les essais hybrides. L'installation d'essai sera raccordée au groupe servo-hydraulique existant de l'ETH. Le fournisseur fournira « toute l'assistance nécessaire à une intégration correcte », y compris la conception hydraulique, le concept de sécurité et la mise au point de la technologie des vannes. La structure mécanique doit pouvoir supporter en toute sécurité des forces extrêmement élevées, offrir une structure de châssis rigide et permettre un réglage hydraulique des traverses. Par ailleurs, il convient de garantir un accès aisé pour la mise en place des éprouvettes, comme le souligne le document : « Un accès aussi aisé que possible […] doit être assuré. » Le montage s'effectuera dans le hall d'essais HIF C 51. La livraison se fera via le HIF C 54, point de livraison 27. Les composants seront livrés par camion et transportés à l'aide des ponts roulants du hall. Les deux ponts roulants ont chacun une capacité de levage de 10 t, une hauteur maximale de crochet de 7,4 m et un écartement minimal entre les crochets de 8 m. En raison de travaux menés en parallèle, la durée d’utilisation est limitée à 3–4 heures. De plus, « la commande des ponts roulants doit être effectuée exclusivement par du personnel formé de l’entrepreneur ». La charge au sol est limitée à 10 kN/m² dans la zone de manutention et à 7 kN/m² dans certaines parties du hangar, complétée par des charges admissibles par roue de 135 kN sur une surface de 0,4 m × 0,4 m. Pour l'installation du chantier, l'entrepreneur met à disposition au moins un conteneur à outils ; aucun local de repos n'est mis à disposition, mais des toilettes le sont. Une visite facultative permet aux soumissionnaires de se familiariser avec les conditions spatiales, sans toutefois répondre à des questions relatives à la procédure. Pour plus d'informations, voir le cahier des charges et les annexes.
description-proc.deu: Der Fachbereich Stahl- und Verbundbau der ETH Zürich plant die Beschaffung einer neuen Universalprüfmaschine für die Bauhalle am Standort Hönggerberg. Die Anlage soll großformatige Bauteile unter realitätsnahen statischen und dynamischen Belastungen prüfen und damit zukünftige Forschungsarbeiten im Stahl-, Verbund- und Erdbebeningenieurwesen unterstützen. Zu den Hauptanwendungen zählen „zentrische und exzentrische Druckversuche […] mit der optionalen Möglichkeit Zugkräfte einzuleiten“. Die Projektleitung liegt bei Dominik Werne, dem Leiter der Bauhalle. Die Maschine muss einen großzügigen Versuchsraum bieten, der Prüfkörper bis „B:1500 mm, H:1500 mm, L:5000 mm“ aufnehmen kann. Einspannhöhen von 500 bis 5000 mm ermöglichen sowohl Druck- als auch Zugversuche. Der Versuchsraum muss vollständig einsehbar sein, um optische Messsysteme wie DIC einsetzen zu können. Die hydraulische Ausstattung umfasst einen Vertikalzylinder mit „10 MN Drucklast, 6 MN Zuglast und 400 mm Zylinderweg“ sowie zwei Horizontalzylinder mit jeweils „1 MN Druck-/Zuglast und 500 mm Zylinderweg“. Die Anlage muss dynamische Versuche bis 10 Hz und Geschwindigkeiten bis 250 mm/s ermöglichen. Eine präzise Steuerung mit mindestens 5 kHz Abtastrate, Güteklasse 1/0.5 sowie modernen digitalen Schnittstellen (z. B. EtherCAT) ist erforderlich, um kraft- und verformungsgesteuerte Versuche sowie Hybrid Testing zu unterstützen. Die Prüfanlage wird an das bestehende servohydraulische Aggregat der ETH angebunden. Der Lieferant stellt „alle erforderliche Unterstützung für eine ordnungsgemäße Integration“ bereit, einschließlich Hydraulikplanung, Sicherheitskonzept und Abstimmung der Ventiltechnik. Die mechanische Struktur muss extrem hohe Kräfte sicher aufnehmen, eine steife Rahmenkonstruktion bieten und eine hydraulische Traversenverstellung ermöglichen. Gleichzeitig ist eine einfache Zugänglichkeit für den Einbau von Prüfkörpern sicherzustellen, wie im Dokument betont wird: „Eine möglichst einfache Zugänglichkeit […] sollte gegeben sein.“ Die Montage erfolgt in der Versuchshalle HIF C 51. Die Anlieferung erfolgt über HIF C 54, Anlieferung 27. Die Bauteile werden per LKW angeliefert und mit den Hallenkranen transportiert. Die beiden Krane besitzen je 10 t Tragfähigkeit, eine maximale Hakenhöhe von 7.4 m und einen minimalen Hakenabstand von 8 m. Die Nutzungsdauer ist aufgrund paralleler Arbeiten auf 3–4 Stunden begrenzt. Zudem gilt: „Die Bedienung der Hallenkrane darf ausschliesslich durch geschultes Personal des Unternehmers erfolgen.“ Die Bodenbelastung ist limitiert auf 10 kN/m² im Umschlagbereich und 7 kN/m² in Teilen der Halle, ergänzt durch zulässige Radlasten von 135 kN auf 0.4 m × 0.4 m. Für die Baustelleneinrichtung stellt der Unternehmer mindestens einen Werkzeugcontainer bereit; Aufenthaltsräume werden nicht zur Verfügung gestellt, Toiletten jedoch schon. Eine freiwillige Begehung ermöglicht es den Anbietern, die räumlichen Gegebenheiten kennenzulernen, jedoch ohne Beantwortung verfahrensbezogener Fragen. Weiterführende Angaben siehe Pflichtenheft und Anhänge.
description-proc.eng: The Department of Steel and Composite Structures at ETH Zurich is planning to procure a new universal testing machine for the construction hall at the Hönggerberg site. The equipment is intended to test large-scale components under realistic static and dynamic loads, thereby supporting future research in steel, composite and earthquake engineering. The main applications include “centric and eccentric compression tests […] with the optional ability to apply tensile forces”. The project is being led by Dominik Werne, Head of the Construction Hall. The machine must provide a spacious test chamber capable of accommodating test specimens up to “B: 1500 mm, H: 1500 mm, L: 5000 mm”. Clamping heights ranging from 500 to 5000 mm allow for both compression and tensile tests. The test chamber must be fully visible to enable the use of optical measurement systems such as DIC. The hydraulic system comprises a vertical cylinder with “10 MN compressive load, 6 MN tensile load and 400 mm cylinder stroke”, as well as two horizontal cylinders, each with “1 MN compressive/tensile load and 500 mm cylinder stroke”. The system must be capable of dynamic tests up to 10 Hz and speeds of up to 250 mm/s. Precise control with a sampling rate of at least 5 kHz, accuracy class 1/0.5 and modern digital interfaces (e.g. EtherCAT) is required to support force- and strain-controlled tests as well as hybrid testing. The test rig will be connected to ETH’s existing servo-hydraulic power unit. The supplier will provide “all necessary support for proper integration”, including hydraulic design, a safety concept and coordination of the valve system. The mechanical structure must safely withstand extremely high forces, provide a rigid frame construction and allow for hydraulic crossbeam adjustment. At the same time, easy access for the installation of test specimens must be ensured, as emphasised in the document: “Access should be as easy as possible […].” Assembly will take place in test hall HIF C 51. Delivery will be via HIF C 54, delivery point 27. The components will be delivered by lorry and transported using the hall cranes. Both cranes have a lifting capacity of 10 t each, a maximum hook height of 7.4 m and a minimum hook spacing of 8 m. Due to work being carried out in parallel, the operating time is limited to 3–4 hours. Furthermore: “The hall cranes may only be operated by the contractor’s trained personnel.” The floor load is limited to 10 kN/m² in the handling area and 7 kN/m² in parts of the hall, supplemented by permissible wheel loads of 135 kN over an area of 0.4 m × 0.4 m. The contractor shall provide at least one tool container for the site facilities; staff rooms will not be provided, but toilets will be. A voluntary site visit will enable tenderers to familiarise themselves with the site layout, though no questions relating to the tender procedure will be answered. For further details, please refer to the specifications and annexes.

title-proc.eng: Traceability of Chemicals in Plastics and in Plastic Products

description-proc.eng: The Nordic program to reduce plastic pollution 2025-2027 under the Nordic Council of Ministers for the Environment and Climate is administered by the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment. The program is launching a call for tenders for a project on the traceability of chemicals in plastics and plastic products. Chemicals of concern in plastics pose significant challenges for health, the environment and the safe functioning of circular value chains. Effective traceability enables regulators and industry to identify and control chemicals of concern, improve the safety and transparency of recycled plastics, strengthen monitoring, reporting and compliance, support accurate classification and control of plastic-related trade and reduce data gaps and inconsistencies across value chains. There is a need for a consolidated global overview of the methods, approaches, and systems currently used to promote traceability of chemicals in plastics and plastic products along value chains. This project aims to identify practical, implementable and globally relevant options for improving the traceability of chemicals in plastics and in plastic products, providing targeted input to the ongoing Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) and supporting future plastic treaty implementation. It is also relevant for targets under the Global Framework on Chemicals, GFC, as well as the Stockholm Convention. The project will consolidate and assess existing regulatory, technical and sectoral approaches across major jurisdictions including the EU, USA, China, Brazil, South Africa and selected Middle Eastern countries, and as far as possible seek to translate these into prioritised recommendations for increased transparency. The outcome will be communicated as a publicly available report. Project output should be issued through NordPub according to the guidelines of the Nordic Council of Ministers. See appendix 1 for more information.

description-proc.eng: Background Lærdalsøyri is the municipal centre in Lærdal municipality and it is subject to flaum from Lærdalselvi. The measures must be ready for planning before they can be engineered and executed. The planning work in question does not include the protection, but also the area necessary for access, construction, rigging, operation, inspection and future maintenance. The planning work must take inspections of the existing buset, industrial works subject, agriculture, infrastructure, landscape, natural values, cultural environment and other interests within and in the local area of the plan area. A plan programme has been prepared for area development. The planning programme was subject to public inspections in the period 22.10.-21.12.2025, and was set by the municipal council on 10 September 2026. The plan programme will set guidelines for the planning process, the implementation, alternatives that shall be assessed and impact assessment as well as the implementation work that shall be carried out. The planning work shall be carried out in close cooperation between Lærdal municipality, NVE, the supplier and other relevant authorities and interested parties. The objective of the assignment The aim of the assignment is to get professional assistance to prepare a complete area development plan for total flaum protection for Lærdalsøyri. The area development plan shall: Clarify the area use for relevant flaum protection measures. Necessary area for the establishment, access, construction, rigging, operation and maintenance of the initiative. Clarify relationship with existing and planned land use Assessed the works for the environment and community Provide a sufficient basis for further detailed engineering design services and execution. Contribute to a dispenser and verifiable plan process. Facilitate co-work with basic entrepreneurs, inhabitants, businesses, organisations and public authorities. Tenderers shall have professional co-ordination between the different parts of the planning work. There shall be decipherable and substantiated consistency between the disciplines, impact assessment, risk and vulnerable lift analysis, the plan chart, the zoning guidelines and the plan review. NVE works parallel to the preliminary project, and it is expected that the supplier cooperates closely with NVE to sikra consistency between the municipality and NVE's planning work.

Le prestataire travaillera en étroite collaboration avec la section E+E, en particulier avec les deux conseillers sectoriels chargés de l’économie et du développement des compétences professionnelles, qui serviront de principaux interlocuteurs. Le prestataire identifiera, sélectionnera et synthétisera les connaissances et les évolutions pertinentes issues de la recherche internationale, des débats politiques, des organisations internationales et des réseaux professionnels, et les transposera dans des formats accessibles et utiles pour les membres. Cela inclut la production de supports de communication et de connaissances, ainsi que la gestion et la mise à jour des principales plateformes numériques, notamment l’environnement Microsoft Teams de la section E+E et le site web du réseau E+E. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. title-proc.eng: Framework agreements for carpentry services

description-proc.eng: Background Troms County needs to establish a new framework agreement for carpentry services for the county ́s owned building in Troms county. The procurement shall ensure a structured and regulatory procurement of ongoing maintenance and repair work within the carpentry and joinery discipline. The county manages comprehensive and assembled buildings, including sixth form colleges, sports halls, dental clinics, administration buildings, student residences and residences that are rented out to their own employees. This gives a regular need for smaller and medium sized work connected to maintenance, replacement and simple constructional adaptations. The objective of the procurement is to ensure available capacity, predictability and good follow-up of such assignments across the county ́s locations. The framework agreement shall also contribute to more efficient call-offs, reduce the need for individual procurements and facilitate uniform handling of assignments within the relevant discipline. It is important for tenderers to be aware that the need includes ongoing assignments of varying sizes and character, divided between several geographical areas in Troms. The assignments will mainly apply to the existing buildings and are connected to ordinary maintenance, improvements and minor adaptations. Description of the assignment The procurement is for a framework agreement for carpentry services for Troms county ́s buildings in Troms county. The delivery shall cover the ongoing need for carpentry and joinery work that occurs during the contract period. The assignments can i.a. include replacing and repairing doors, windows, walls, ceilings, floor details and fixed fittings, as well as minor construction work and adaptations. Minor external work can also be required, such as simple constructions and minor entries connected to the existing buildings and outside areas. The works shall be able to be ordered both as assignments carried out in accordance with hours used and as minor assignments at the agreed fixed price within the specified amount limits. Where necessary for the execution of the assignment, the delivery can also include consumables and accompanying materials that are naturally included in the execution. The contract shall not be used for the procurement of materials alone. The framework agreement shall cover needs across the county ́s entities and locations, and must therefore be suitable for assignments of varying extent, complexity and geographical location. Further requirements for the delivery, limitations to other disciplines and terms for call-offs will be in the tender documentation in general. Typical assignments will be carpenter/carpenters, floors, doors, ceilings, fixtures etc. and can include replacing windows, replacing door blades, assembling new doors as well as minor construction work such as erection of roofs over bicycle parking or simple sheds. Carpentry services shall include; Assembly, replacement and repair of doors, sills and fittings. Work on walls, ceilings and internal building constructions.
